headline: Cannabis week ahead: Georgia licence window, Illinois hemp hearing
dek: From 16 to 23 November: Georgia takes dispensary bids, a judge weighs Illinois hemp limits, Glass House reports and the Russell list updates.
key_points: Georgia's medical cannabis commission takes dispensary licence applications from 16 to 20 November, with the patient registry a few hundred names short of unlocking a tenth store per producer.
On 19 November a federal judge hears a bid to block Illinois' hemp THC limits, and the top military appeals court hears a challenge to how service members are convicted of THC use.
Glass House Brands and Rubicon Organics report third-quarter results on 16 November; FTSE Russell updates its preliminary index additions on 20 November.
Rhode Island's adult-use retail application window and Oregon's comment period on new hospice rules both close on 23 November.
body: The second week after the midterms is light on votes and heavy on deadlines. Licence windows open in Georgia and close in Rhode Island, a federal judge takes up a challenge to Illinois' new hemp limits, and two listed cannabis companies report. Below is MetaFlora's calendar for 16 to 23 November, with the decisions that follow into December.
All dates come from regulators, courts, company releases or the reporting linked at the end. Times are local to each event.
## Monday 16 November: Georgia opens, Oregon hears, Glass House reports

Georgia's Access to Medical Cannabis Commission opens a special dispensing licence window from 16 to 20 November, announced by executive director Andrew Turnage at the commission's 4 November meeting, CannabisNews.org reported. Only the state's six existing producers, two Class 1 and four Class 2, can apply. Under Georgia's Hope Act each producer may add one store for every 10,000-patient rise in the registry. The registry stood at 64,243 on 4 November, a few hundred short of the 65,000 mark that would raise the cap to 10 stores per producer, or up to 60 statewide. The commission's licence register lists dispensing licences numbered up to 30, the last six approved on 4 November, four of them for TheraTrue's True Bliss brand and two for Trulieve.

In Oregon, the Health Authority holds a virtual hearing at 9 a.m. Pacific on rules that let hospice and residential care patients use medical cannabis on site. We cover those rules in a separate story this morning.

After the market close, Glass House Brands reports third-quarter results, and Rubicon Organics reports the same day, IgniteIt reported. In Europe, Luxembourg's tender to buy medical cannabis oils and flower closes on 16 November, according to Cannabis Thérapeutique.

U.S. District Judge Martha Pacold hears a request for a temporary restraining order and preliminary injunction against the Illinois Hemp Act, The Marijuana Herald reported. The suit, from the Illinois Healthy Alternatives Association and five businesses, targets the law's 0.4-milligram total THC cap per container outside licensed dispensaries. As we reported on 10 November, the state agreed not to enforce the law against the plaintiffs and covered members until the hearing. A ruling either way will be read by every state now writing its own hemp limits.

The same day, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Armed Forces hears oral arguments in United States v. Lawrence, a challenge to the legal inference used to convict service members of wrongful THC use, the Herald reported. Los Angeles also holds a webinar on 19 November explaining its 4 December retail storefront lottery for social equity applicants.
> This week tests the two levers states are pulling at once: opening licensed retail and closing the hemp side door.

FTSE Russell publishes an updated preliminary list for its December reconstitution. Trulieve and Glass House were both on the first preliminary list of Russell 3000 additions, as we reported on 14 November. Further updates follow on 27 November and 4 December, and confirmed changes take effect after the close on 11 December, IgniteIt reported. For both stocks, staying on the list would bring index-fund buying; dropping off would remove an expected source of demand.

Rhode Island's Cannabis Control Commission closes its adult-use retail licence portal at 4 p.m. Eastern, with final zoning approval among the documents due, according to The Marijuana Herald. The state is expanding the number of licensed retailers beyond its current operators. Oregon's written comment period on the hospice rules also closes, at 5 p.m. Pacific.

The calendar tightens after Thanksgiving. The DEA expects medical cannabis businesses operating under temporary federal authorisation to have compliant supply chains by 29 November, under guidance the Herald described as nonbinding. Missouri's research facility licensing rules take effect on 30 November. New Connecticut rules on hemp-derived cannabinoids for the licensed market take effect on 1 December.

On 4 December, Curaleaf's bid for Aurora Cannabis is set to expire unless extended, Cannabis Thérapeutique reported, as Organigram's rival agreed deal awaits shareholder and court approval. Planet 13 shareholders vote on the company's merger with Vireo Growth on 10 December, according to Planet 13, the same day DEA comments on 2027 production quotas close. The federal hemp definition and government funding both reach their deadline on 11 December.

None of this week's events is likely to move the whole sector alone. Together they show where the action is between elections and the new Congress: in licensing offices, district courts and index committees. The Illinois hearing is the one most likely to produce a surprise, and the Georgia registry count is the one to watch for a quick change in store numbers.
